reason: I want to make a place to sit and work; bricks and metal seem useful for a supporting structure.
expectation: I expect them to form a sturdy base or work surface, though I don't know the exact result.

alternatives.reason: Felt and fabric could make a cushion, but a supporting structure seems like a useful first step.

effect: The bricks and metal made a bench with a seat and worktop, so it now needs whatever the remaining materials can provide.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the salvaged materials become a useful place by the window.
reason: Felt and fabric are the only available combination, and they seem suited to making the bench more comfortable.
expectation: I expect them to make a cushion or covering, though I don't know whether it will be fitted to the bench yet.

effect: The felt and fabric made a cushion, which can now be fitted to the bench.
reaction: The springy felt is a satisfying finishing touch for the seat.
reason: Putting the cushion on the bench is the only available combination and should complete the seating area.
expectation: I expect a cushioned window bench, possibly completing the goal.

effect: The cushion completed the window bench and the chapter's goal, giving the cabin a place to sit and work.
reaction: The image of watching the sunset from the padded seat is a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the bench from bricks and salvaged metal was most worthwhile: it connected earlier work to a practical place in the cabin.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the cushion was predictable once both pieces existed, though it provided a natural finish.

surprise.text: The bench included a worktop as well as a seat, making it more useful than I initially expected.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the materials and their uses were straightforward.

continue.text: I would continue to see how life on Mars develops, though this short chapter offered little new understanding beyond assembling familiar materials.
